It is important to address how corporations offload the responsibility of maintaining adequate staffing onto their current employees. When companies fail to hire enough staff and instead heap endless duties onto the few workers on the floor, it creates immense pressure that inevitably degrades the customer experience. 

If a customer receives inaccurate information or has a frustrating interaction, the blame shouldn't fall on the retail worker, who is likely overworked and under-resourced. The employer bears the ultimate responsibility for creating these environments, yet the public often targets the employees instead. We need to stop holding workers accountable for the systemic failures of corporate management. comments.text: Customers, you cannot force and demand stock/inventory into existence. It’s in stock when it is stocked. This customer should have been asked to leave and trespassed if they did not leave. If you demand it this bad and you can’t find it anywhere else, $60 for the toy. How bad do you want it? You want two? Price just went up to $100. $60 for the first, $100 for the second. You want to buy all of them??? You’re gonna wipe out our entire stock? I’ll cut you a bulk purchase discount; since $100 is the new market price, I’ll sell all of them to you for $95 each. If they’re willing to pay it, this is what you call a free market this is the effective demand of that product. To tractor supply, either one of these scenarios is a win. If someone wants to film on private property and trash talk the company and the employees, distracting and preventing the employees from being productive, this is a customer that brings no value to the company-this is protecting the company. Real time inflating the price if its in the shipment, if sold, tractor supply would be impressed with the employees’ business sense and generating amazing profit margins. When a single person wipes out an entire shipment of Pokémon cards or these toys or whatever, it signals to the company, hey…we can increase this items price much more until it balances out the supply demand. This is exactly why companies will implement dynamic pricing. The companies want the profit for their product, they don’t want customer’s to profit from reselling.
